bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Volatile global outlook - macroeconomic, geopolitical and currency exposure — Given its global footprint, diversified service portfolio and increasing participation in large transformation programmes, the Company is exposed to macroeconomic, geopolitical, regulatory, cybersecurity, delivery, talent and contract-management risks. Interest-rate movements, currency fluctuations, trade and tariff pressures, geopolitical conflict and energy-price volatility can influence customer spending, delivery costs and supply-chain stability across markets. Mitigated through quarterly management reviews, internal audits, proactive risk monitoring, supply-chain de-risking and operating discipline across business units.
- Technology obsolescence and execution risk from rapid technology-led change — Developments in Industry 4.0, agentic AI, connected infrastructure, cloud, cybersecurity and digital engineering require continuous investment in skills, platforms and delivery models - technology-led change presents both opportunity and execution risk. Mitigated through structured technology-practice plans, R&D investment across geographies, expanding AI and cybersecurity capabilities and continuous team training.
- AI governance, privacy, data-security, ethical-use and accountability risk — AI is a defining growth opportunity but organisations that scale AI without adequate controls may expose sensitive information, create operational vulnerabilities or weaken decision governance. The Company is addressing this through AI training, internal policy development, responsible solution design and a formal AI usage framework aligned with its AI-first strategy, and is refining its AI governance policy.
- Cybersecurity - one of the most critical risks for a managed service provider — As the Company executes larger and more complex contracts it must protect customer environments and its own; it strengthens data protection, operational resilience, contractual safeguards and cyber-insurance coverage, supported by 24x7x365 monitoring of IT assets with leading tools, weekly security alerts and awareness checklists, controlled access and device binding, continuous patching, periodic vulnerability scanning of Digital Desk and Company websites, and continuous review of customer contracts for security obligations, risk allocation and insurance adequacy.
- Compliance risk across multiple countries, including data protection — Operating across multiple countries, non-compliance with legal, regulatory, labour, tax, data-protection and contractual requirements may result in legal exposure, financial penalties, operational disruption or reputational impact. Managed through defined ownership across sales, business units and corporate functions, periodic monitoring of regulatory changes, third-party specialists in selected jurisdictions, maintenance of certifications such as ISO, CMMI and PinkVERIFY, upgraded core platforms (SAP, Salesforce) and preparation for the Digital Personal Data Protection Act.
- Delivery risk and receivables / payment delays — Delivery risk arises when service commitments, quality standards, response timelines or customer expectations are not met in a highly competitive managed-services market where customers expect continuous improvement, automation-led efficiency and measurable value. Mitigated through shift-left automation, analytical dashboards, disciplined pricing, delivery governance and active service monitoring. Payment delays remain a global operational concern, with the finance team managing receivables through structured follow-up and cash-flow discipline.
- Contract-management risk — Risk may arise from unclear scope, changing customer expectations, complex delivery dependencies or evolving commercial terms; mitigated by standardising contract structures where appropriate, strengthening contract administration, improving understanding of customer environments and continuously refining contracts in line with service obligations and risk-allocation requirements.
- Employee-related risk - attrition and specialised skill scarcity in a talent-driven business — As a service-centric, talent-driven organisation, the ability to attract, develop and retain specialised talent is essential to competitiveness; attrition, skill scarcity and changing workforce expectations can affect delivery continuity and cost efficiency. Mitigated through cross-training, global and domestic recruitment models, collaboration with internal and external recruiters, leadership strengthening, skill-development programmes and close delivery oversight.

business.body:
- Self-described as "a publicly listed global leader in Information Technology consulting and services, with a legacy dating back to 1984", operating as "a trusted Managed Services Provider and Master Systems Integrator".
- Claims a first-mover position in Indian smart cities: "we became the first company to execute a Smart City project with the successful delivery of the Pune City Surveillance project in 2015"; the scale slide shows 14 Smart / Safe Cities.
- Customer-base credentials on the scale slide: 175 Number of Customers and 10 Fortune 100 Customers; a later slide instead says "We proudly partner with several Fortune 500 companies" (the deck uses both formulations).
- Service portfolio spans five stated pillars - AI Ops & Automation, Cloud Infrastructure Services, Cyber Security & Networking, Software Services and Digital Workplace Services - plus Digital Engineering Solutions (Master Systems Integration, Safe/Smart City, IBMS, IoT, command and control, image analytics).
- The Chairman frames the current phase around "integrated capabilities across managed services, digital infrastructure, cloud, cybersecurity and AI-led transformation" in an environment where "macroeconomic uncertainties and evolving geopolitical developments continue to influence discretionary technology spending".
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [New engagements] Entry into a new service line is claimed: an Enterprise Application Services engagement with "a leading NYSE-listed electronic design and test solutions company" covering ServiceNow, Jitterbit and Boomi, which "marks Allied Digital's entry into the Enterprise Application Services space".
- [New engagements] Other wins listed: end-to-end Workplace Services for a customer-owned (mutual) bank in Australia across Melbourne, Sydney and Adelaide; a turnkey System Integrator project from the Department of School Education, Government of Punjab for an Integrated Command and Control Centre; managed services for a Government of India organisation under the Ministry of Commerce; IT Asset Management for an international property consulting firm; and IT infrastructure support for "one of India's leading FMCG companies".
- [Renewals] "Renewed multiple strategic customer engagements across the pharmaceuticals, chemicals, real estate, BFSI, medical devices and retail design sectors" - the deck gives no contract values, durations or order book for any win or renewal.
- [FY26 one-off] The FY26 EBITDA figure of Rs. 112 cr is footnoted "* Excluding one-time provision of Rs. 36 Cr in FY26"; the deck does not say what the provision relates to.
- [Corporate history] Acquired EnPointe Global Services LLC in 2008 to expand US presence; converted to a public limited company and listed on BSE and NSE in 2007; the Chairman is described as leading the company "through Version 6.0".
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: ADSL began as one of India's early third-party IT infrastructure support providers and has evolved into a global IT consulting and services company delivering managed services, systems integration, digital workplace services, enterprise infrastructure transformation, cybersecurity, digital engineering, smart infrastructure and AI-Ops-led automation. It serves enterprises and government bodies across more than 70 countries, combining one-time Solutions (project-based implementations) with recurring annuity Services contracts that provide margin stability and customer retention. Its business model is shifting from conventional technology services toward platform-led, AI-enabled and outcome-oriented engagements, with roughly 20% of FY2025-26 revenue generated from smart city projects for government customers.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Cloud and Infrastructure Services:** Cloud enablement across AWS, Azure, GCP and hybrid environments, Infrastructure modernisation, containerisation and microservices architecture, Disaster recovery and continuous infrastructure monitoring
- **Cybersecurity and Networking:** AIM 360 framework (prevention, detection, response, compliance), Security Operations Centres (SOC) with SIEM and SOAR, Zero Trust Architecture, SASE and endpoint detection and response, Identity and access management, ransomware protection and compliance frameworks, DPDP-readiness and OT security consulting
- **Digital Workspace Services:** 24x7 multi-channel, multi-lingual service desk operations, End-user computing, endpoint lifecycle management and global logistics, Cognitive support frameworks and analytics-driven workflow optimisation
- **AI Ops and Automation:** Digital Desk (AI-Ops-based ITSM/ESM no-code and low-code platform, rebranded from ADiTaaS in 2024), Digital Desk Bot Platform, 3A framework (Automation, Analytics, Agility), Agentic AI platform architecture, AI, machine learning, generative AI and robotic process automation (RPA), Low-code/no-code platforms, DevOps integration and enterprise applications
- **Digital Engineering Solutions:** Smart and Safe City solutions with integrated command and control centres, Intelligent building systems and operational technology (OT) integration, Real-time data platforms enabling predictive insights and automation, Computer vision, IoT and video analytics solutions

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- A '10x growth strategy' targeting sustained annual growth of more than 25% over the long term, supported by a multi-pronged plan across geographic expansion, AI-first service transformation, data-centre opportunities, public-place technologies, computer vision, digital twins and global cybersecurity consulting
- Continue geographic expansion across Japan and EMEA markets
- Advance an AI-first strategy across service lines, enterprise AI, automation solutions and AI governance, including deployment of the Company's own agentic AI platform architecture and ready-to-deploy use cases
- Strengthen offerings in data-centre build and infrastructure services for AI workloads
- Acquire new customers in public-place technologies by leveraging emerging capabilities in computer vision and digital twins
- Expand the cybersecurity consulting practice across global markets, extending the portfolio beyond OT security into consulting, assessment, implementation and DPDP-readiness support
- Shift the business model from conventional technology services toward platform-led, AI-enabled and outcome-oriented engagements, with Digital Desk as a key pillar of the platform strategy
- Grow the share of enterprise-led and recurring annuity managed services to improve revenue visibility, earnings stability and customer retention
- Realign technology capabilities into five focused service towers: enterprise infrastructure IT services (including cloud); digital engineering services (smart cities, computer vision, IoT); digital transformation (AI and automation); cybersecurity services and network solutions; and digital workplace services
- Pursue smart city, safe city and industrial-zone opportunities using command-centre expertise and systems-integration capability, and extend that capability base into adjacent enterprise and industrial computer-vision use cases
- Refine pricing, delivery and operating models to stay commercially competitive as competition intensifies and customers focus on cost optimisation, balancing pricing discipline with margin protection and AI-led delivery efficiencies
- Invest in architecture capability, platform innovation, automation frameworks, deeper engineering expertise, leadership depth and governance frameworks to support a more scalable operating model
- The Company's stated governance philosophy is to achieve business excellence and dedicate itself to increasing long-term shareholder value while keeping in view the needs and interests of all stakeholders, with an emphasis on transparency and business ethics. On distributions, the Notice of the Thirty-Second AGM (to be held September 01, 2026) places the declaration of a dividend on equity shares for the financial year ended March 31, 2026 as ordinary business for members' approval. This bundle does not otherwise set out a dividend, buyback or reinvestment policy.
- Energy-conservation efforts have contributed to approximately 20% year-on-year savings, alongside optimisation of water consumption and more efficient waste-management practices
- Tree-planting initiatives support broader environmental stewardship
- The Company plans this year to actively formalise its sustainability initiatives into a global measurable report
- The Company intends to leverage its ESG initiatives to strengthen brand credibility and stakeholder trust
- Emerging technologies such as AI and blockchain are to be deployed with appropriate governance, privacy and sustainability considerations; the Company is refining its AI governance policy and progressing toward compliance with India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act
- Governance and employee-engagement mechanisms: a comprehensive Whistleblower Policy encouraging confidential reporting, accessible grievance redressal through online and offline channels, an Open-Door Policy, and structured onboarding covering Company policies, the Code of Conduct and ADSL's Core Value Pyramid
- Zero tolerance policy for sexual harassment at the workplace with an Internal Committee constituted under POSH 2013; the disclosure table reports 0 complaints received, 0 disposed and 0 pending beyond ninety days (the table is captioned as being for the financial year ended March 31, 2025 within this FY2025-26 report)
- Compliance with the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961 including paid maternity leave, nursing breaks and protection from dismissal, with no discrimination in recruitment or service conditions on grounds of maternity
- Gender composition of the workforce as on March 31, 2026 disclosed under diversity, equity and inclusion principles: 1,883 male employees, 208 female employees and nil transgender employees
- Stated commitment to leveraging technology to benefit all segments of society, drive financial inclusion and promote sustainable and responsible use of resources
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: ADSL is an asset-light IT services business, and its expansion narrative is about footprint, partnerships, platforms and capability rather than plants or capacity. Geographic expansion is being pursued into newer geographies to increase addressable markets: the Company is evaluating partnerships in Japan, has established new partnerships in Mauritius to address opportunities in Mauritius and Africa, and continues to explore inorganic growth opportunities globally; the stated strategy also includes continued expansion across Japan and EMEA markets. Strategic global partnerships are being built with leading technology players - the recent addition of IBM as a strategic partner has already contributed to a large FMCG opportunity, with several additional opportunities being pursued through that collaboration. The sales and delivery engine has been expanded through senior sales leadership added in the US, a broader sales organisation, a new leader for the India managed services business, a refreshed digital presence and a global implementation of Salesforce for lead tracking, pipeline management and sales governance. Platform build-out continues around Digital Desk, the proprietary low-code/no-code enterprise service management platform, which now manages more than 6 million support tickets annually at an average first-time resolution rate of approximately 87%, while the AIM 360 cybersecurity framework has been extended through an assessment platform aligned with NIST-based industry controls and computer-vision applications are being expanded beyond smart cities into enterprise environments. Capability expansion includes training more than 100 key resources in AI, evaluating multiple AI platforms, assessing voice-to-text and text-to-voice technologies for virtual AI agents, and developing new business models and innovative pricing structures. The Company has defined a clear roadmap for the next three to five years aligned with its longer-term ambition to build a business ten times its current scale, and states that it strategically increased leverage by securing additional financing facilities during the year to fund its long-term project pipeline and accelerate group-level growth. No plant, capacity or rupee capex quantum is disclosed in this material.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Enterprises have moved decisively to make AI operational, with agentic AI gaining rapid acceptance; enterprises invest in AI to reduce operating costs, improve end-user experience and strengthen decision-making
- Data sovereignty has become a core requirement, driving demand for local data centres, sovereign cloud environments and secure infrastructure for AI workloads - creating opportunities in data-centre build, cloud migration, technology operations and managed services
- Cybersecurity remains a priority as regulatory, operational and geopolitical risks increase; the Digital Personal Data Protection Act is expected to gain prominence as compliance deadlines approach, and OT security remains critical for manufacturing, FMCG and industrial businesses
- AI governance, data classification, data governance and data security are becoming standard requirements for application upgrades, while multi-cloud strategy, workload migration and cloud FinOps remain in demand
- Smart manufacturing is evolving from IoT-enabled monitoring to AI-driven autonomous operations (autonomous maintenance, closed-loop process optimisation, dynamic digital twins, flexible robotics), creating opportunities to extend digital engineering, computer vision and automation into industrial environments
- Government investment in digital governance, urban mobility, surveillance infrastructure and citizen-centric public services is a long-term opportunity; approximately 20% of FY2025-26 revenue came from smart city projects for government customers
- Growing opportunities across data centre modernisation, intelligent workplaces, operational technology integration, smart cities and digital infrastructure programmes are expected to remain important drivers of technology spending over the coming years
- Revenue mix shift toward enterprise-led and recurring managed services engagements improves revenue visibility, earnings stability and quality of growth; services-led engagements offer stronger retention and better operating leverage as relationships scale
- Margin levers cited: higher contribution from annuity-led managed services, greater utilisation of global delivery capabilities, and increasing adoption of automation, AI-led delivery frameworks and proprietary platforms
- Operating leverage is expected to improve progressively as the business scales beyond the ₹1,000 crore annualised revenue run-rate milestone
- Headwinds: the industry continues to face pricing pressure and customers remain focused on cost optimisation and cost control; FY2025-26 was challenging for India-based enterprises
- The financial year was challenging for the IT industry due to macroeconomic factors including the conflict in the Middle East, immigration-related challenges in the US and US tariff announcements
- One-time provisions in FY26 (expected credit losses, asset verification and other matters arising from the auditor-led review) were largely non-recurring; with these legacy matters substantially addressed, management expects future profitability to increasingly reflect operating strength rather than exceptional adjustments
- The Board's Report states the outlook for FY2026-27 remains positive with continued growth prospects for the IT industry in terms of underlying demand, and the Company foresees significant demand growth from its IT business
- Customers increasingly evaluate technology through operational resilience, uptime, automation, observability and business outcomes rather than implementation milestones, favouring partners able to manage the full digital infrastructure lifecycle
- Approximately ₹166 crore of orders and renewals were secured in the fourth quarter of FY26 alone, reflecting broad-based demand across digital transformation, infrastructure modernisation, managed services and AI-led solutions
- The Company continued to convert its order pipeline into active execution, improving future revenue visibility
- The Company enters FY2026-27 with a healthy pipeline of sizeable opportunities and expects several active deals to progress toward closure in the early quarters; the pipeline is expected to strengthen through the remainder of the year
- Key business wins during the year: a five-year end-user services contract from a leading global pharmaceutical company headquartered in Europe for its global operations
- A global end-user services contract from a leading New York-based fashion brand
- A three-year enterprise infrastructure services contract from a large premium investment-management company based in New York, USA
- A five-year subcontract to provide service desk and end-user field services for a well-known global offshore oil drilling company operating out of Texas, USA
- A five-year contract from a leading insurance company in India for end-user services, asset management, the Digital Desk platform and AI-enabled automation
- A five-year end-user service desk contract being delivered for a leading global IT services and consulting company
- A five-year comprehensive safe-city project, including a command centre, awarded by the Government of Maharashtra for an industrial zone - described as a significant safe-city order for industrial zones
- The Company successfully renewed key agreements and secured high-volume Smart/Safe City project contracts during the year

deepdive.thesis: Allied Digital achieved record revenue (Rs. 968 Cr, +20% YoY) and resolved critical audit qualifications regarding inter-corporate loans, clearing the path for institutional confidence. Growth is pivoting toward high-margin Enterprise AI and Managed Services, with a robust Rs. 2,000 Cr+ government pipeline in Maharashtra expected to rebound in FY27 despite Q4 delays caused by geopolitical equipment cost volatility.

open.item: The Company enters FY2026-27 with a healthy pipeline of sizeable opportunities and expects several active deals to progress toward closure in the early quarters, with the pipeline strengthening through the remainder of the year as macroeconomic conditions improve by end of the second quarter.

The Board has recommended a dividend of ₹1.50 per share of ₹5 each (30% of equity share capital) for the year ended March 31, 2026, absorbing ₹847.71 lakhs of cash, payable to members on the register as on August 28, 2026.
The Company has embarked on a 10x growth strategy targeting sustained annual growth of more than 25% over the long term.
The Company is targeting ₹1,000 crore of revenue, having closed FY2025-26 at an exit run rate of ₹1,000 crore on annual revenue of ₹968 crore.

The Company has strengthened its sales and marketing engine - adding senior sales leadership in the US, expanding the sales organisation, appointing a new leader for the India managed services business and globally implementing Salesforce - initiatives expected to improve market visibility, customer engagement and conversion discipline.

The Company is augmenting advanced workflow capabilities to transform IT processes and enable autonomous virtual agents, having developed the first version of its agentic AI architecture, piloted it with selected customers, evaluated multiple AI platforms and trained more than 100 key resources in AI.

The Company continues to build strategic partnerships with leading global technology players, with IBM recently added as a strategic partner that has already contributed to a large FMCG opportunity and through which several additional opportunities are being actively pursued.

The Company is actively expanding into newer geographies - evaluating partnerships in Japan, having established new partnerships in Mauritius to address Mauritius and Africa, and continuing to explore inorganic growth opportunities globally.

risks.note: Given its global footprint, diversified service portfolio and increasing participation in large transformation programmes, the Company is exposed to macroeconomic, geopolitical, regulatory, cybersecurity, delivery, talent and contract-management risks. Interest-rate movements, currency fluctuations, trade and tariff pressures, geopolitical conflict and energy-price volatility can influence customer spending, delivery costs and supply-chain stability across markets. Mitigated through quarterly management reviews, internal audits, proactive risk monitoring, supply-chain de-risking and operating discipline across business units.
risks.risk: Volatile global outlook - macroeconomic, geopolitical and currency exposure

risks.note: Developments in Industry 4.0, agentic AI, connected infrastructure, cloud, cybersecurity and digital engineering require continuous investment in skills, platforms and delivery models - technology-led change presents both opportunity and execution risk. Mitigated through structured technology-practice plans, R&D investment across geographies, expanding AI and cybersecurity capabilities and continuous team training.
risks.risk: Technology obsolescence and execution risk from rapid technology-led change

risks.note: AI is a defining growth opportunity but organisations that scale AI without adequate controls may expose sensitive information, create operational vulnerabilities or weaken decision governance. The Company is addressing this through AI training, internal policy development, responsible solution design and a formal AI usage framework aligned with its AI-first strategy, and is refining its AI governance policy.
risks.risk: AI governance, privacy, data-security, ethical-use and accountability risk

risks.note: As the Company executes larger and more complex contracts it must protect customer environments and its own; it strengthens data protection, operational resilience, contractual safeguards and cyber-insurance coverage, supported by 24x7x365 monitoring of IT assets with leading tools, weekly security alerts and awareness checklists, controlled access and device binding, continuous patching, periodic vulnerability scanning of Digital Desk and Company websites, and continuous review of customer contracts for security obligations, risk allocation and insurance adequacy.
risks.risk: Cybersecurity - one of the most critical risks for a managed service provider

risks.note: Operating across multiple countries, non-compliance with legal, regulatory, labour, tax, data-protection and contractual requirements may result in legal exposure, financial penalties, operational disruption or reputational impact. Managed through defined ownership across sales, business units and corporate functions, periodic monitoring of regulatory changes, third-party specialists in selected jurisdictions, maintenance of certifications such as ISO, CMMI and PinkVERIFY, upgraded core platforms (SAP, Salesforce) and preparation for the Digital Personal Data Protection Act.
risks.risk: Compliance risk across multiple countries, including data protection

risks.note: Delivery risk arises when service commitments, quality standards, response timelines or customer expectations are not met in a highly competitive managed-services market where customers expect continuous improvement, automation-led efficiency and measurable value. Mitigated through shift-left automation, analytical dashboards, disciplined pricing, delivery governance and active service monitoring. Payment delays remain a global operational concern, with the finance team managing receivables through structured follow-up and cash-flow discipline.
risks.risk: Delivery risk and receivables / payment delays

risks.note: Risk may arise from unclear scope, changing customer expectations, complex delivery dependencies or evolving commercial terms; mitigated by standardising contract structures where appropriate, strengthening contract administration, improving understanding of customer environments and continuously refining contracts in line with service obligations and risk-allocation requirements.

As a service-centric, talent-driven organisation, the ability to attract, develop and retain specialised talent is essential to competitiveness; attrition, skill scarcity and changing workforce expectations can affect delivery continuity and cost efficiency. Mitigated through cross-training, global and domestic recruitment models, collaboration with internal and external recruiters, leadership strengthening, skill-development programmes and close delivery oversight.
risks.risk: Employee-related risk - attrition and specialised skill scarcity in a talent-driven business
